title: private-deployments-bundle-optimizer-playtest
content:
Objective:
Quick playtest of a pricing + support bundle optimizer for private deployments (on-prem vs VPC vs hybrid). Purpose is to produce: 1) a compact scenario grid that sales/solutions can run live during demos, 2) recommended bundle structures (term/commit/support tiers) that maximize ARR while preserving payback < 18 months in typical mid-market accounts, and 3) ops-level levers customers can adopt to reduce TCO by 15-35% without changing core HW choices.

Executive summary (1 paragraph):
Early runs show that a 36-month commit with a 12–18 month hardware amortization window, combined with a moderate support uplift (Silver) and a 20% assumed inference-efficiency uplift from Redwood Optimize recommendations, yields payback between 10–16 months for typical mid-market customers (20–50 p50 GPUs). VPC-only proposals win on time-to-deploy for customers without strict data residency, but on-prem with 3rd-party co-lo offers better long-term unit economics when customers can take advantage of existing colo capacity.

Assumptions (tab: Assumptions):
- HW unit: p4d-equivalent instance; replace with customer-specific SKU where known.
- On-prem CAPEX includes: HW purchase, rack+power provisioning, network aggregation, initial install services (one-time).
- VPC includes: cloud reserved instances or dedicated host pricing + egress estimates.
- License model: base platform fee (annual) + per-GPU serving fee (monthly) + embedding/token-rate uplift (usage).
- Support tiers: Bronze (email, 9x5), Silver (24/7 on-call + quarterly reviews), Gold (SLA-backed, dedicated CSM + faster RTO windows).
- Efficiency levers assumed: 20% baseline (caching + batching), +10–25% with quantization/compile changes depending on model family.
- Tax/finance: straight-line depreciation over amortization window; assume 0% capital tax credits for simplicity (fill with country-specific values later).

Key formulas used (single-line, placed into grid):
- Total first-year cost (on-prem) = HW_capex + install_services + (annual_license) + (support_fee) + infra_opex_year1
- Total first-year cost (VPC) = reserved_compute_year1 + storage + network_egress + annual_license + support_fee
- Monthly unit cost per GPU = (Total annual cost / 12) / effective_gpu_count (after consolidation and batch factor)
- Payback months = (Customer_contract_value_initial_commit * discount_rate_adjusted) / incremental_annual_ops_savings

Notes on the grid: replace commas in numeric cells with locale-appropriate separators when dropping into spreadsheets. The example numbers are illustrative. Two knobs sales should tune live: efficiency_uplift (0.0–0.35) and reserved_compute_year1 (commit/term negotiation).

Amortization tab (Amortization):
- Sample straight-line schedules included for 24 / 36 / 48 month windows.
- Compute a monthly depreciation line and push into the P&L slice we present to finance.
- Quick check formula: monthly_depr = HW_capex / amort_window_months; add to monthly fixed cost.

Bundle recommendations (tab: BundleRecommendations):
- Package A (Starter): 12-mo term, low commit, Bronze support, 8% platform discount, no install uplift. Targets: early-stage AI-native startups.
- Package B (Growth): 24-mo term, mid commit (30% GPU commit), Silver support, 15% platform discount, 1x install credit applied. Targets: mid-market.
- Package C (Enterprise Optimized): 36-mo term, high commit (60% GPU commit), Gold support, 20–25% platform discount + free fourth-week onboarding services and quarterly SRE runbooks. Includes optional private network peering credit.

Pricing levers that move unit economics (for negotiation):
- Term length (12/24/36): longer = lower annual license; encourage 36 for minimum on large deals.
- Commit level: convert reserved_compute_year1 into effective unit price; use sliding scale discounts.
- Install credits vs. upfront price: defer a portion of install as credits applied monthly to reduce payback.
- Support uplift: price as % of license or flat fee; flatten to % for easier modeling.
- Hardware financing option: Redwood financing program (partner) spreads CAPEX over 36 months; include financing rate in model.

Ops playbook (tab: OpsPlaybook) - practical steps customers can take (and how Redwood helps):
- Consolidate model variants onto fewer larger GPUs where latency allows (saves 10–18% at scale).
- Apply continuous batching and prefix cache for chat-heavy workloads (reduces token cost 12–25%).
- Adopt recommended quantization profile from Redwood Optimize; expect +8–20% throughput depending on model.
- Use KV cache warmup windows and preheat scripts during business hours to avoid cold-start penalties.
- Regularly profile per-route inefficiencies via Console and apply per-route batch sizing.

Runbook snippet for a typical 50-GPU on-prem account:
- Day 0: Hardware acceptance + network smoke test.
- Day 1–7: Redwood agent install, model sync, baseline perf run (capture tail latency and throughput), apply 1st round Optimize suggestions.
- Month 1: Efficiency review with Solutions Eng + apply quantization/compile changes.
- Quarterly: Business review + bundle true-up (commit vs actual).

Customer-facing talking points (one-liners):
- On-prem: best long-term unit economics if you have colo leverage; ideal when data residency or regulatory constraints exist.
- VPC: fastest delivery and simplest ops; good for proof-of-concept and ramp.
- Hybrid: combine fast ramp via VPC with long-term economics via on-prem swap when capacity stabilizes.

Unresolved items / TODOs (notes to self):

- Validate financing APR for partner leasing program (Liam).
- Add example with token-heavy embeddings workload (Ethan).
- Add country-specific tax credits (deferred).

Appendix: quick-copy formulas for the sheet (paste into cells):
- =SUM(HW_capex,Install_services,Annual_license,Support_fee,Infra_opex_year1)
- =IF(Deployment="VPC",Reserved_compute_year1,HW_capex/Amort_months + Infra_opex_year1)
- Effective_gpu_count = Provisioned_GPUs * (1 - consolidation_savings) * (1 + burst_factor)

Next steps and immediate action items:
- Convert this playtest into a live Google Sheet with param controls (slider for efficiency_uplift, select for term, numeric input for commit). Owner: Asha Kapoor. Due: 2026-03-01.
- Add sample deals (3 anonymized customers) to validate payback sensitivities. Owner: Mariana. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Ship a stripped-down interactive version to sales enablement (1-page cheat sheet + two scenario templates). Owner: Liam. Due: 2026-03-15.

Notes: keep numbers conservative for first external share. This doc intentionally mixes qualitative negotiation guidance with a compact scenario grid sales can tweak in meetings. Replace placeholders with customer SKUs before sending externally.

Footnote: this is a working playtest — expect iterative changes after initial deal pilots.
